taxonomy:
Below is a taxonomy of the listed **grid-based logic games**, using **only the rules provided**. I group them by the **primary action the solver performs** and then note important subtypes based on rule structure.

---

# Taxonomy of the listed grid-based logic games

## I. Shading / coloring puzzles
These puzzles primarily ask the solver to decide which cells are black/colored/shaded and which remain white.

### A. Illumination-based shading
- **Akari**  
  Place light bulbs in white cells; bulbs illuminate rows/columns until blocked by black cells or frame.

### B. Binary black/white cell determination
- **Chained Block**  
  Fill cells so black-cell blocks satisfy size/shape/chain conditions.
- **Choco Banana**  
  Paint cells black so black connected cells form rectangles/squares, while white connected cells do not.
- **Hitori**  
  Color cells black to remove repeated numbers in rows/columns; black cells cannot touch; white cells stay connected.
- **Kurodoko**  
  Color cells black; numbered white cells count visible white cells up to black cells or frame.
- **Kurotto**  
  Color cells; circle numbers give sums of continuous black cells extending orthogonally.
- **Norinori**  
  Place black cells in consecutive pairs; each bold region contains exactly two black cells.
- **Nurikabe**  
  Fill cells black/white; numbered white islands have given sizes; black cells form one connected wall and no 2×2.
- **Nuritwin**  
  Shade cells so each region contains exactly two shaded blocks of equal size; all shaded cells globally connected.
- **Sto-stone**  
  Fill colored cells black under room constraints; after “dropping” downward, stones fill the bottom half.
- **Tilepaint**  
  Color entire tiles black or white; diagonal clues count black cells to right/down; final image forms an object.
- **Usowan**  
  Fill cells colored/uncolored with adjacency numbers, except one wrong clue per bold region.
- **Yajilin**  
  Black cells are determined alongside a loop; arrow clues count black cells in a direction.

### C. Room-constrained shading
These are shading puzzles where bold-line areas are central to the rules.
- **Heyawake**  
  Paint cells in rooms by room counts; black cells nonadjacent; white cells connected; white runs cannot cross more than two rooms.
- **LITS**  
  Shade tetrominoes, one per region; same tetromino shapes cannot touch edge-to-edge; all shaded cells connected; no 2×2.
- **Nurimeizu**  
  Paint whole rooms black or white; white cells form a maze from S to G with shortest-path constraints on circle/triangle rooms.

### D. Shading with local shape constraints
- **Shakashaka**  
  Place triangular black pieces in cells so remaining white areas form rectangles/squares.
- **Nurimisaki**  
  Fill cells black/white so circled white cells are “Misaki” promontories, with line-length clues and no 2×2 in either color.

---

## II. Loop-drawing puzzles
These ask for a **single loop**, usually through cell centers or along grid edges.

### A. Cell-center single-loop puzzles
The loop passes through cells rather than along edges.
- **Dotchi-Loop**  
  Single loop through cells; white circles must all be straight or all turns within a bold area; black circles avoided.
- **Masyu**  
  Single loop through all black/white circles with straight/turn behavior determined by circle color.
- **Mid-loop**  
  Single loop through cells; black circles are midpoints of straight loop segments.
- **Moon-or-Sun**  
  Single loop through rooms, entering each room only once; in each room uses all moon cells or all sun cells, alternating by room.
- **Nagareru**  
  Single directed loop through black arrow cells; movement constrained by wind from black cells.
- **Suraromu**  
  Single loop through cells crossing all “gates”; open circle gives number of gates to cross; some gates are order-numbered.
- **Yajilin**  
  Single loop through non-black, non-number cells; black cells also satisfy directional count clues.

### B. Edge-based single-loop puzzles
The loop is drawn on the lattice edges between dots/cell borders.
- **Slitherlink**  
  Connect adjacent dots to make one loop; numbers tell how many surrounding edges are used.

---

## III. Path / line connection puzzles that are not a single loop
These involve drawing paths or lines, but not necessarily one loop.

### A. Pair-connection path puzzles
- **Numberlink**  
  Connect matching numbers with non-crossing paths through cells.

### B. Object-to-target routing / movement paths
- **Yosenabe**  
  Move circles in straight lines into gray areas; arrows show movement; gray-area numbers equal sums of entering circles.
- **Satogaeri**  
  Move circles within countries so each country ends with one circle; numbered circles move exact distances without crossing tracks.

### C. Line extension from marked objects
- **Pencils**  
  Mark pencils and draw lines from pencil tips; numbers in pencils indicate pencil length and line length from tip.

---

## IV. Region-division / partition puzzles
These require dividing the grid into regions or blocks by drawing boundaries or assigning cells to regions.

### A. Partition into arbitrary blocks with size constraints
- **Five Cells**  
  Divide the grid into blocks of exactly five cells; clues count surrounding block lines.
- **Shikaku**  
  Divide the grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains one number equal to its area.
- **Sashigane**  
  Divide the grid into one-cell-wide L-shaped blocks; circles indicate knees, arrows indicate ends, some with size clues.
- **Double Choco**  
  Draw borders to divide the grid into blocks; each block contains matching white and gray areas of the same shape.

### B. Partition into number-defined polyominoes
- **Fillomino**  
  Fill cells with numbers so same-number connected blocks have size equal to the number; equal-sized blocks cannot touch.
- **Makaro**  
  Fill rooms with 1 up to room size; arrowed black cells indicate where the largest adjacent number is; equal numbers cannot touch across rooms.
- **Ripple Effect**  
  Fill rooms with consecutive numbers starting at 1; equal numbers in row/column must be spaced by at least their value.
- **Sudoku**  
  Fill 9×9 grid with 1–9 so each row, column, and 3×3 block contains all digits.

---

## V. Placement puzzles on cells
These involve placing symbols, numbers, or marks into cells rather than shading or drawing paths.

### A. Symbol placement
- **Juosan**  
  Fill every cell with either — or |, under territory balance conditions and run-length restrictions.
- **Evolomino**  
  Place squares in cells to form blocks associated with arrows; blocks along an arrow evolve by adding one square without rotation/flip.

### B. Number placement / fitting
- **Nansuke**  
  Fill blank cells with numbers from a given list; entries run horizontally or vertically.
- **Hebi**  
  Place snake numbers 1 to 5 in white cells, creating sequential snakes under adjacency and “field of view” constraints.

---

## VI. Area-formation / shape-construction puzzles
These focus on building or identifying connected areas with specified forms.

### A. Connected-area shape matching
- **Double Choco**  
  Each divided block contains white and gray areas with the same shape.
- **Nuritwin**  
  Each region contains two shaded blocks of equal size.
- **Chained Block**  
  Black blocks are classified by size and shape, and connected by corner-touching chains with no repeated size-shape type in a chain.
- **LITS**  
  Regionwise tetromino construction with shape-adjacency restrictions.

### B. Rectangle/square formation or avoidance
- **Choco Banana**  
  Black connected areas must be rectangles/squares; white connected areas must not.
- **Shakashaka**  
  White uncovered parts must be rectangles/squares.
- **Shikaku**  
  Entire solution is a partition into rectangles.

---

## VII. Visibility / directional-clue puzzles
These use line-of-sight, arrow direction, or orthogonal extension as the main clue mechanism.

- **Akari** — bulbs illuminate in rows/columns.
- **Hebi** — snake “view” from 2→1 direction cannot see another snake before a black square/frame.
- **Kurodoko** — numbered cells count visible white cells to nearest black or frame.
- **Kurotto** — circle numbers sum continuous black-cell rays in four directions.
- **Nagareru** — wind blows from black arrow cells and constrains path direction.
- **Makaro** — arrowed black cells indicate which adjacent cell has the maximum number.
- **Tilepaint** — diagonal clues count black cells to the right/downward.
- **Yajilin** — arrows count black cells in a direction.
- **Yosenabe** — circles move directionally in straight lines into gray areas.

---

## VIII. Adjacency / connectivity constrained puzzles
Many puzzles rely strongly on global connectivity or forbidden adjacency; these can be cross-classified as follows.

### A. White cells must be connected
- **Heyawake**
- **Hitori**
- **Kurodoko**
- **Nurimisaki**

### B. Black/shaded cells must be connected
- **Nurikabe** (black wall connected)
- **LITS** (colored cells connected)
- **Nuritwin** (all shaded cells connected)

### C. Black/shaded cells may not touch orthogonally
- **Heyawake**
- **Hitori**
- **Kurodoko**
- **Usowan**
- **Yajilin**

### D. No 2×2 shaded/black formations
- **Nurikabe**
- **LITS**
- **Nuritwin**
- **Nurimeizu** (neither color can form 2×2 or larger squares)
- **Nurimisaki** (neither color can form 2×2 or larger squares)

---

# Compact classification by primary solving action

## 1. Shade/color cells
Akari, Chained Block, Choco Banana, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Kurotto, LITS, Norinori, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki, Nurikabe, Nuritwin, Shakashaka, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Usowan, Yajilin

## 2. Draw a single loop
Dotchi-Loop, Masyu, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Slitherlink, Suraromu, Yajilin

## 3. Draw non-loop paths/lines
Numberlink, Pencils, Satogaeri, Yosenabe

## 4. Divide the grid into regions/blocks
Double Choco, Five Cells, Fillomino, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Sashigane, Shikaku, Sudoku

## 5. Place symbols or numbers in cells
Evolomino, Hebi, Juosan, Nansuke

## 6. Connect objects in a network
Hashiwokakero

---

# Special singleton class

## Network-construction puzzle
- **Hashiwokakero**  
  Connect numbered islands with one or two bridges, no crossings, making one connected network.  
  This is neither a loop puzzle nor a region-partition puzzle; it is best treated as a **graph/network construction** puzzle.

---

# Notes on overlap
Several games naturally belong to more than one category:

- **Yajilin** = shading puzzle + single-loop puzzle + directional clue puzzle.
- **Double Choco** = region-division puzzle + shape-matching puzzle.
- **LITS** = shading puzzle + polyomino/shape puzzle + connectivity puzzle.
- **Nurimeizu** = shading puzzle + maze/path-structure puzzle.
- **Makaro**, **Ripple Effect**, **Sudoku**, **Fillomino** all involve number placement, but differ by whether the key structure is rooms, polyomino-like regions, or Latin-square constraints.

If you want, I can also turn this into:
1. a **tree diagram**,  
2. a **table with one primary category per puzzle**, or  
3. a **multi-label matrix** showing every puzzle against features like loop / shading / rooms / numbers / connectivity / arrows / polyominoes.
